question: When Fidelity Charitable's FYE 6/2026 Form 990 (expected in the IRS TEOS index around May 2027, going by its 2024-05-15, 2025-05-14 and 2026-05-18 submissions) is mirrored, rerun scripts/mission_net_payout.py and the Schedule I top-line comparison to find the recipient lines that make up the CY2025 'significant outlier granting totaling $727 million'. Compare them with the FY2025 lines (NPT $346.8m, JHU $340.3m, ImpactAssets $203.7m, GS PF $159.9m)
conclusion_affected: Sponsor-reported grant statistics net of DAF-to-DAF transfers; whether the CY2025 outlier was a DAF-to-DAF move
rationale: CY2025 spans Fidelity's FY2025 (Jan–Jun 2025) and FY2026 (Jul–Dec 2025). The FY2026 return is not filed yet, so the outlier cannot be located from public data before then

question: Measure post-SPLC-hold DAF-to-DAF outflows. When the FYE 6/2026 and FYE 6/2027 returns of Fidelity, Vanguard and DAFgiving360 are mirrored (about May 2027 and May 2028), compare their Schedule I lines to community foundations and other sponsors with the FY2021–FY2025 baseline in net-payout-by-sponsor.csv. Before then, use calendar-year 2026 returns of the recipient community foundations only for their aggregate Schedule D contributions, which do not name the source
conclusion_affected: Portability lock-in; whether discretion complaints become switching
rationale: Only FY2027 (Jul 2026–Jun 2027) is a clean post-hold window for June-FYE sponsors. FY2026 mixes nine pre-hold months with three post-hold months. Recipients' Schedule B donor detail is redacted in public XML

question: Recover sponsor-to-sponsor transfers for the sponsors whose Schedule I is a single 'see attached' line (RCF, BofA CGF, NY Community Trust, Greater Horizons, Greater Kansas City CF, US Charitable Gift Trust, Donors Fund, Stifel, Fund for Charitable Giving). Use the attached grant lists in ProPublica or IRS PDF images (human retrieval if gated), then add the transfers to net-payout-by-sponsor.csv
conclusion_affected: Net payout of national and community-foundation segments (about 5% of beginning DAF assets is excluded)
rationale: 130 sponsor-years point Schedule I to an attachment. They are excluded from the net-payout sample, which removes RCF ($4.2bn) and BofA CGF ($3.8bn) from the national segment

question: Build a reviewed recipient whitelist for 'DAF-to-DAF' that drops panel EINs receiving program grants, not DAF transfers: universities and hospitals such as JHU, Harvard and Cornell, which are DAFRC 'sponsors'; religious denominations and federations; and affiliated pairs such as Dechomai Asset Trust → Dechomai Foundation. Use it to replace the three nested tiers with one audited definition
conclusion_affected: Net-payout point estimate (tier_a 22.8% versus tier_c 20.2% on FY2021–24 pooled)
rationale: Tier_c ($43.5bn) is more than double tier_b ($27.9bn), mostly because of grants to university and religious 'sponsors'. Tier_a misses CF and processor recipients. The gap between tiers is the main uncertainty in the estimate
